legal.title: 📋 Legal notice & GDPR
legal.controller: Filenymous is open-source software. Files travel directly from one browser to the other (WebRTC) and are never stored by the publisher: there is no file database. Each user remains responsible for the files they share.
legal.data: To connect the two browsers, a signaling server temporarily exchanges the transfer code and network connection details (IP addresses, WebRTC parameters). When a direct connection is impossible, a TURN relay forwards the already-encrypted bytes (AES-256-GCM) without being able to read or keep them. Nothing is persisted. The browser and OS name (e.g. “Chrome · Windows”) is exchanged only between the two peers. No cookies, no ads; only anonymous audience measurement (see below).
legal.audience: We use Umami, an open-source analytics tool that we host ourselves (OVHcloud VPS in Europe, www.opendpe.net): no data is shared with third parties. It sets no cookie and stores nothing in your browser. For each page view it only receives the page path (e.g. “/app/”, never the part after “#” or “?”, so never your links, keys, codes or passwords), the address of the page you came from, without parameters or fragment, the language and screen size, and derives the browser, OS, device type and country/region from the request. Your IP address is used for that and for a hashed visit identifier renewed every day; it is not stored. Nothing is measured on the secret and whistleblowing (report) pages. If your browser sends “Do Not Track” or “Global Privacy Control”, nothing is sent. Legal basis: legitimate interest (aggregated visit statistics); you can also block www.opendpe.net/umami/ with a content blocker.
legal.erasure: Since nothing is stored on a server, there is nothing to erase on the publisher’s side: closing the sender’s tab ends the share and makes the link useless. The decryption key only exists inside the shared link.
legal.hosting: The site is hosted by OVHcloud (France). The signaling and TURN relay servers run on an OVHcloud VPS in Europe; they never see file contents.
legal.terms: Files are shared directly between browsers, with no server storage. Only send files you have the right to share, only share links with recipients you know, and do not use Filenymous for illegal or harmful content. By sending a file, you confirm that you understand and accept these terms.

privacy.title: Privacy: what is protected, and what is not
privacy.e2ee: Content (files, names, notes) is encrypted in the browser (AES-256-GCM). The key only exists in the link, after “#”, which browsers never send to the server.
privacy.ram: Nothing is stored on a server or in browser storage: content lives in the memory of the host's and participants' tabs and is wiped when the wall is destroyed, when the host leaves, or on close.
privacy.relay: The signaling relay never sees the key, the password, the wall name or the content: only an opaque wall id and WebRTC connection parameters. It keeps no access log for walls, but sees your IP address during the connection (in-memory rate limiting).
privacy.ip: This is not anonymity: with WebRTC, the host sees each participant's IP address and each participant sees the host's (unless a TURN relay is used).
privacy.tor: To hide your IP address, use a trusted VPN; Tor Browser disables WebRTC and cannot be used for the wall.
privacy.whistle: For a sensitive report (source, whistleblower), prefer the whistleblowing channel, which works with Tor Browser:
privacy.screens: Destroying the wall wipes in-memory copies, not what a participant already downloaded, copied or photographed.
privacy.live: Live streams (screen, camera, mic): only after you agree, relayed by the host's tab over encrypted WebRTC connections (DTLS-SRTP) negotiated inside the encrypted channel; the host sees the stream, the relay never does.
privacy.agents: AI agents: off by default. When the host allows them, everything an agent reads is sent to its AI model provider, outside end-to-end encryption. The “AI” badge is self-declared.
